samples.summary: `safeEnvelope` breaks the issue's "forwarded verbatim" acceptance criterion (and the doc row that says "(forwarded)") by rewriting the upstream envelope
samples.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:61` states the acceptance criterion: "A backend-shaped body (e.g. TYPE_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED) is still forwarded verbatim, exit code 1, from *every* command". The plan (lines 21-51) asks only for a shape guard (`isErrorEnvelope`) that forwards the documented envelope or throws `UpstreamHttpError`. The implementation adds an unrequested sanitizing layer on the forward path: `code` truncated to 80 chars (formatter.ts:162), `message` truncated to 500 chars with an ellipsis (formatter.ts:123-125), a `message` starting with `<` replaced by `HTTP <status>` (formatter.ts:122, 165), and all sibling fields (e.g. the documented `command` field on `ApiError`) dropped once the serialized body exceeds 4000 bytes (formatter.ts:167-170). Consequently the design-doc row it added — `docs/design/cli.md:1042` "Backend error body *is* the envelope | 1 | (forwarded) | (the upstream's own code …)" — describes behavior the code does not implement for large or HTML-bearing envelopes. Either the criterion should be renegotiated in the todo/design doc, or the caps dropped; as it stands the shipped pass-through is not verbatim and is not what any spec text describes.

samples.summary: The new truncation/HTML-drop policy on the envelope path is documented nowhere (README §Errors or cli.md §10), the exact failure the task's own lessons file calls out
samples.evidence: Acceptance criterion 4 of the originating todo requires `packages/cli/README.md` and `docs/design/cli.md`'s error matrix to document `HTTP_ERROR` "since it is a code agents may branch on", and the lessons file (`docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-lessons.md:31-35`) says "A contract nobody documented is a contract nobody can rely on". `HTTP_ERROR` is documented (README.md:116-130, cli.md:1041-1055), but the new observable behaviors — a 500-char `message` cap with a trailing `…`, an `error.message` that is an HTML document being replaced by `HTTP <status>`, an 80-char `code` cap, and sibling fields silently dropped past 4000 bytes — appear in no doc. An agent parsing stderr can observe all four.
searchedFor: grep HTTP_ERROR / UNAUTHORIZED across packages/cli and docs

samples.summary: The envelope shape is now declared twice: the pre-existing `ApiError` interface (unreferenced) and the new inline predicate type in formatter.ts
samples.evidence: `http-client.ts:26-32` exports `interface ApiError { error: { code: string; message: string; command?: string } }` — a grep across `packages/cli` finds no other reference to it. The new guard re-declares the same contract inline (`formatter.ts:76-85`, `safeEnvelope`'s parameter at `formatter.ts:158-161`). The repo expects reuse and the lessons file explicitly wants "the envelope contract in one file"; either `ApiError` should be the reused type (and re-homed next to `outputError`) or removed as dead, rather than leaving two independent definitions of the same wire shape.

samples.summary: The §8.1 exit-code contract rewrite (0/1 only, `2` reserved, † footnotes on YORKIE_ERROR/FONT_LOAD_ERROR) exceeds this issue's scope and pre-empts a separately tracked finding (#586)
samples.evidence: The originating todo's only doc requirement is that README and cli.md's error matrix document `HTTP_ERROR` (todo lines 66-67). This diff additionally rewrites §8.1's exit-code semantics and annotates two unrelated planned codes as unshipped. `docs/tasks/active/20260729-autonomous-issue-hunting-todo.md:103` lists "#586 — documented exit code 2 for system errors is never produced" as its own filed finding, so the exit-code contract belongs to that issue's change, not this one. Not harmful, but it retires a documented public contract (exit 2 for auth/system errors) under an unrelated PR.

samples.summary: Doc comment and README state an absolute invariant ("Every command that talks to the backend routes its `!res.ok` branch through here" / "Every command reports the same code") that `login` does not satisfy
samples.evidence: `formatter.ts:203-208` and README.md:123-126 assert the invariant without qualification, but `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62,79,96` still call `fetch` directly and print bare prose ("Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP 403). Try again with `wafflebase login`") with `process.exit(1)` and no envelope at all. The todo lists login's workspace fetch as an explicit non-goal (todo:72-73), so the code is right and the absolute wording is wrong; a reader auditing the contract will trip on it.

samples.summary: URL construction is now inconsistent within one client: `apiKeysUrl()` encodes the workspace id, `base` (used by every other call) does not
samples.evidence: `apiKeysUrl()` (line 385) builds `${server}/workspaces/${encodeURIComponent(this.config.workspace)}/api-keys` while `base` (line 84) interpolates `this.config.workspace` raw. Same input, two escaping policies in the same class — pick one (ideally a shared `workspacePath()` helper) so the two bases cannot drift.

samples.summary: Skill files that enumerate the codes a command can emit were not updated with `HTTP_ERROR`
samples.evidence: `skills/docs-read-content.md:83-89` and `skills/slides-read-content.md:70` document `TYPE_MISMATCH` for their content commands; only `docs-import-docx.md:84` and `slides-import-pptx.md:72` list `HTTP_ERROR`. Since every content/export command can now emit `HTTP_ERROR`, the read-content skills are slightly stale. The todo's acceptance names only README + cli.md, so this is a taste call, not an unmet criterion.

finding.summary: `safeEnvelope` breaks the issue's "forwarded verbatim" acceptance criterion (and the doc row that says "(forwarded)") by rewriting the upstream envelope
finding.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:61` states the acceptance criterion: "A backend-shaped body (e.g. TYPE_MISMATCH, SESSION_EXPIRED) is still forwarded verbatim, exit code 1, from *every* command". The plan (lines 21-51) asks only for a shape guard (`isErrorEnvelope`) that forwards the documented envelope or throws `UpstreamHttpError`. The implementation adds an unrequested sanitizing layer on the forward path: `code` truncated to 80 chars (formatter.ts:162), `message` truncated to 500 chars with an ellipsis (formatter.ts:123-125), a `message` starting with `<` replaced by `HTTP <status>` (formatter.ts:122, 165), and all sibling fields (e.g. the documented `command` field on `ApiError`) dropped once the serialized body exceeds 4000 bytes (formatter.ts:167-170). Consequently the design-doc row it added — `docs/design/cli.md:1042` "Backend error body *is* the envelope | 1 | (forwarded) | (the upstream's own code …)" — describes behavior the code does not implement for large or HTML-bearing envelopes. Either the criterion should be renegotiated in the todo/design doc, or the caps dropped; as it stands the shipped pass-through is not verbatim and is not what any spec text describes.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described and is reachable from both forward paths. `safeEnvelope` (formatter.ts:158-171) is invoked by `forwardUpstreamError` (:225) and `upstreamErrorJson` (:250), and it rewrites the upstream envelope: `code` sliced to 80 (:94, :162), `message` sliced to 500 with an appended ellipsis (:90, :123-125), a `message` starting with `<` nulled (:122) and replaced by `HTTP <status>` (:165), and all sibling fields dropped when the serialized body exceeds 4000 bytes (:106, :167-170). The originating task's acceptance criterion (todo.md:61-63) says a backend-shaped body is "still forwarded verbatim ... from *every* command", and the Plan (todo.md:21-51) asks only for the `isErrorEnvelope` shape guard plus `UpstreamHttpError` — no clamping is requested, and Non-goals (todo.md:69-73) do not cover it. The design-doc row added at docs/design/cli.md:1042 says "(forwarded)" with "the upstream's own code"; grepping docs/design/cli.md for verbatim/clamp/truncat/4000/bounded/HTML and packages/cli/README.md:116-126 shows no doc anywhere describes the 80/500/4000 caps or the HTML substitution (`MAX_UPSTREAM*`/`safeEnvelope`/`clampUpstreamText` appear only in formatter.ts). So this is a genuine unmet acceptance criterion plus a design-doc/implementation divergence and unrequested scope beyond the stated Plan — both squarely in the design-fit lane and `major` per the rubric. No guard makes it unreachable and no named refutation ground applies; the strongest counter-argument (that small TYPE_MISMATCH/SESSION_EXPIRED envelopes do pass through untouched) is a renegotiation of the criterion, which is exactly the remedy the finding requests, not a refutation.

finding.summary: The two new Error Matrix rows contradict the rows and prose they sit next to instead of reconciling them. Immediately below, `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM` and above, `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`; §8.1 (cli.md:780-782) and packages/cli/README.md:127-128 both state `2` = system error (network, auth). The behaviour this delta generalises to *every* backend command is exit `1` with `HTTP_ERROR` (or a verbatim envelope) for 401/403/5xx alike — `forwardUpstreamError`/`outputError` only ever set `process.exitCode = 1` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:62,175). Since the PR is the change that makes this the universal path and it edits the very table that records the contract, the stale exit-2 rows should have been folded in or removed; as it stands the canonical design doc describes two mutually exclusive behaviours for the same HTTP responses and an agent branching on exit code (which the doc explicitly invites) gets it wrong.
finding.evidence: cli.md:1039-1041 new rows say exit 1 / HTTP_ERROR; cli.md:1038 `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED`; cli.md:1042 `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM`; cli.md:780-782 `2` system error (network, auth).

verdict.reason: The contradictory rows the finding cites do not exist in docs/design/cli.md. There is no `Backend 401/403 | 2 | UNAUTHORIZED` row (cli.md:1038 is `Output file already exists | 1 | FILE_EXISTS`) and no `Backend 5xx or network | 2 | SYSTEM` row (cli.md:1042 is `Backend error body *is* the envelope | 1 | (forwarded)`; 5xx and network are cli.md:1044-1045, both exit 1). A grep of the entire docs/ tree for `UNAUTHORIZED` yields a single hit — cli.md:1052 — which states the opposite of the claim: "There is deliberately no `UNAUTHORIZED` code". No `SYSTEM` code appears anywhere in docs/. The only exit-2 rows are Yorkie/Fontkit (cli.md:1046,1048), both dagger-footnoted at cli.md:1050-1052 as "Planned, not shipped: no path in packages/cli/src sets an exit code of 2 … Every failure the CLI currently produces exits 1". §8.1 (cli.md:780-784) does not say 2 = system error today; it says 2 "is reserved for a future system-error split (network, auth) and is not emitted by any command today — a network or auth failure exits 1 … branch on the envelope's code, not the exit code". packages/cli/README.md:127-130 says the same. The code half of the finding is accurate (formatter.ts:62,226 set process.exitCode = 1) but it agrees with the doc rather than contradicting it, so the alleged stale-contract / mutually-exclusive-behaviour defect is absent.

finding.summary: Unrelated scope creep: a frontend visual-harness font-waiting rewrite is bundled into a CLI error-envelope change
finding.evidence: The diff's stated subject is the CLI upstream-error forwarding helpers (`forwardUpstreamError` / `upstreamErrorJson` in packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts) applied across docs/notes/slides/files. The hunk in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs is a wholly separate concern: it expands VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES with Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono, adds a VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS matrix, adds a catch-all `status !== 'loading'` poll, and relocates `waitForFontsReady(page)` from before the harness-root wait to after the section-ready wait (capturePass). It shares no module, no test, and no acceptance criterion with the CLI work, and it materially changes when screenshots are taken in the visual-baseline lane (a change that can shift/invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines described in docs/design/harness-engineering.md). It should be its own change so it can be reviewed and baselined independently.

verdict.reason: The scope-creep finding is anchored on a font-waiting rewrite in packages/frontend/scripts/verify-visual-browser.mjs that does not exist in the tree. (1) VISUAL_FONT_FAMILIES at line 336 is still exactly ["Noto Sans KR","Noto Serif KR","Nanum Gothic","Roboto"] — no Inter/Fraunces/JetBrains Mono (those strings appear in 17 other files, e.g. font catalogs and index.html, but not in this script). (2) A repo-wide grep for VISUAL_FONT_WEIGHTS returns no matches anywhere. (3) A repo-wide grep for `status !== 'loading'`/`status !== "loading"` returns no matches; the poll at lines 360-369 is an existing fonts.check() waitForFunction. (4) The claimed relocation is inverted: waitForFontsReady(page) is called at line 393, BEFORE the harness-root wait (395-396) and before the section-ready loop (398-402), so the asserted "changes when screenshots are taken / can invalidate the ~220 pinned baselines" mechanism is absent. The diff subject is indeed the CLI upstream-error envelope work (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md), but with none of the four described visual-harness edits present there is no unrelated hunk to unbundle. Not-present in all specifics the finding relies on.
